posts.caption: I guessed this bench was three arm spans long. Two and a bit. My extremely confident measuring unit seems to have variable settings.
posts.translationZh: 我猜這張長椅有三個臂展長，結果是兩個多一點。我這套自信滿滿的測量單位，看來有點不穩定。
posts.imageAlt: Felix estimates the length of an empty riverside bench with his outstretched arms.
posts.storyContext: During lunch, Felix guesses the length of a riverside bench before checking it with his arm span. His estimate is generous, and shifting his feet makes his chosen unit less consistent than he expected. He can discuss everyday estimates, the usefulness of rough measurements, or how he would check his result with a piece of string.

posts.caption: I got a clean run with the skipping rope after work. Then my hood string joined in. Very keen, terrible timing.
posts.translationZh: 下班後跳繩好不容易連續跳順了，帽繩就跑來湊熱鬧。熱情值得肯定，時機真的不太行。
posts.imageAlt: Finn securing a loose hood string after skipping on a sports terrace.
posts.storyContext: Finn has a short skipping session on an empty sports terrace after work. A loose hood string catches his rhythm, so he stops to tuck it away before continuing. He can discuss finding time for brief exercise, the lengths of rope he prefers, or the unexpectedly fiddly clothing details that interrupt a good run.

posts.caption: After work, I bought roasted chestnuts. One shell won't open, so tonight's snack now includes a tiny engineering problem.
posts.translationZh: 下班後買了烤栗子。有一顆怎樣都剝不開，於是今晚的點心多了一道小小工程題。
posts.imageAlt: Hugo pauses under a covered arcade with a paper bag of roasted chestnuts.
posts.storyContext: Hugo buys a small bag of roasted chestnuts after work as the evening turns chilly. Most shells open easily, but one stubborn nut makes him slow down and find a better grip. He keeps the broken pieces in the bag instead of dropping them. He can talk about seasonal snacks, difficult food packaging, or whether the smallest chestnut is worth the effort.

posts.caption: A coat shadow became my after-work film project. The empty sleeve keeps entering like a dramatic villain.
posts.translationZh: 一件外套的影子成了我下班後的拍片計畫。空空的袖子每次晃進畫面，都像大反派登場。
posts.imageAlt: Iris records the moving shadow of a hanging coat in an empty theatre storeroom.
posts.storyContext: Iris notices a hanging coat casting a theatrical shadow while putting equipment away after work. A slight draft moves the sleeve, so she records a short clip with her phone. She starts imagining a scene built entirely from objects. She can discuss atmosphere in films, accidental characters, or what sound would suit the moving shadow.

posts.caption: I chose the thinnest poetry booklet for the journey home. It has already made me miss the sentence I was halfway through thinking.
posts.translationZh: 我挑了最薄的一本詩集準備回家路上讀。才看一下，就忘了自己剛剛在腦中想了一半的那句話。
posts.imageAlt: Isla holds a small plain poetry booklet in a quiet secondhand reading room.
posts.storyContext: Isla stops in a secondhand reading room after work and picks a thin poetry booklet for the ride home. One short poem interrupts an ordinary thought, so she decides to read only a little at a time. She can discuss short books that take longer than expected, commuting reading choices, or whether a poem benefits from being reread immediately.

posts.caption: Three ceiling lights landed in a puddle while I waited out the shower. A very small constellation, with rather unreliable stars.
posts.translationZh: 躲雨時，三盞頂燈落進了水窪，成了我的迷你星座。只是這幾顆星有點不穩定。
posts.imageAlt: Luna watches three small light reflections in a puddle beneath an empty bus shelter.
posts.storyContext: Luna waits under a bus shelter after work while a short shower passes. Three ceiling lights reflect in a shallow puddle, and passing drops keep breaking their arrangement. She watches without photographing it at first. She can discuss patterns in rainy evenings, invented constellations, or the small things that make waiting feel shorter.

posts.caption: My jacket puffed up like a sail on the reservoir path. I zipped it properly and immediately became less interesting to the wind.
posts.translationZh: 走到水庫步道上，我的外套被風吹成一面帆。拉鍊好好拉上後，風馬上就對我沒那麼感興趣了。
posts.imageAlt: Max fastens his windblown jacket on a quiet reservoir path beside dry reeds.
posts.storyContext: Max takes a brisk walk beside the reservoir after work. A gust fills his half-open jacket, making the easy stretch suddenly feel like resistance training. He stops to fasten it and keeps going as daylight fades. He can compare windy walks, sensible layers, and how much weather changes a familiar route.

posts.caption: I stopped to look at a mended basket on my lunch break. The repaired bit was holding its shape better than the rest.
posts.translationZh: 午休時，我停下來看一只補過的編織籃。補過的那一小塊，居然比其他地方還挺。
posts.imageAlt: Maya examines a repaired woven basket in an otherwise empty craft display alcove.
posts.storyContext: During lunch, Maya notices a handwoven basket in a quiet craft display alcove. A patch around its rim is firmer than the older weave, and she spends a few minutes following how the strands join. She likes that the repair remains visible. She can talk about useful objects that get repaired, different weaving patterns, or what makes an ordinary household item worth keeping.

posts.caption: I shelled peas while dinner warmed up. One rolled under the bowl, and I spent longer finding it than shelling the last handful.
posts.translationZh: 等晚餐熱好的時候，我順手剝豌豆。有一顆滾到碗下面，找它花的時間比剝最後那一把還久。
posts.imageAlt: Noah shells peas into a ceramic bowl beside his kitchen window at dusk.
posts.storyContext: Noah shells a small bowl of peas after work while dinner warms on the stove. One pea rolls beneath the bowl, leading to an unnecessarily careful search across the counter. He finds it before clearing up. He can discuss quiet cooking tasks, favorite easy dinners, or the tiny interruptions that make a slow evening memorable.

posts.caption: The pastry came with a fork folded in the napkin. I spent a minute looking for cutlery while holding the answer.
posts.translationZh: 點心附的叉子藏在摺好的餐巾裡。我握著答案，卻花了一分鐘找餐具。
posts.imageAlt: Oscar unfolds a plain napkin to reveal a small fork beside a pastry bag on a cafe ledge.
posts.storyContext: On his lunch break, Oscar looks for a fork before eating his pastry at a cafe window ledge. It turns out to be tucked inside the folded napkin he is already holding. He unwraps it and sets the napkin beside the bag. He can discuss things overlooked in plain sight, small lunch routines, or why he checked everywhere except his own hand.

posts.caption: My lunch bread froze into one solid brick. I only need two slices, but the whole loaf seems keen to join me.
posts.translationZh: 午餐的麵包凍成了一整塊。我只需要兩片，但看來整條都想跟我走。
posts.imageAlt: Ryan gently works two frozen bread slices apart on a workplace pantry counter.
posts.storyContext: Ryan discovers that the sliced loaf he stored in the workplace freezer has stuck together. He rests it briefly on the pantry counter and eases two slices apart rather than tearing them. He can talk about practical freezer habits, preferred lunch fillings and the small food preparations that save trouble later.

posts.caption: The cable clip works. I know because I've now dropped the cable on purpose far more often than I ever did by accident.
posts.translationZh: 線材固定夾有效。我確定，因為現在故意放手測試的次數，已經比以前不小心掉下去還多了。
posts.imageAlt: Theo tests a plain cable clip at the edge of an empty office desk.
posts.storyContext: At the end of the workday, Theo sticks a simple clip under his desk edge to keep a charging cable within reach. The fix works, but testing it becomes an oddly absorbing activity. He can discuss desk annoyances, removable adhesives and which tiny adjustments are actually worth keeping.

posts.caption: I rolled my yoga mat up after work. It quietly unrolled again while I was finding the strap. I respect its patience.
posts.translationZh: 下班後，我把瑜伽墊捲好。找束帶的空檔，它又默默攤開了。我佩服它的耐心。
posts.imageAlt: Yuna reaches for a slowly unrolling yoga mat on a bench in an empty studio corridor.
posts.storyContext: After a short solo stretch after work on Friday, Yuna rolls up her yoga mat in an empty studio corridor. She turns to find its strap and the roll quietly opens again on the bench. She can discuss simple stretches, the trick of keeping a mat rolled and how she winds down after the working week.

posts.caption: I packed my sandwich very securely. At lunch, I discovered I'd also secured the cling film to absolutely everything.
posts.translationZh: 我的三明治包得非常牢。到了午休才發現，保鮮膜也跟所有東西都黏得非常牢。
posts.imageAlt: Zoe holds a partly unwrapped sandwich in an empty workplace break alcove.
posts.storyContext: Zoe unwraps her homemade sandwich in the work break alcove and finds that the film has folded back on itself several times. She gets it free with most of the filling still in place. She can talk about overenthusiastic food packing, her preferred sandwich fillings and whether a lunch box would have been simpler.

posts.caption: My rain gauge has a new spot beyond the sprinkler. I checked it with a measured splash first. Very small science before work.
posts.translationZh: 雨量筒搬到灑水器噴不到的位置了。我上班前先倒了定量的水測試一下，小小做個實驗。
posts.imageAlt: Ada calibrating a homemade rain gauge in a sheltered service passage.
posts.storyContext: Ada has moved her homemade rain gauge away from the sprinkler that confused yesterday's reading. Before work, she checks its scale with a small measuring cup in a sheltered passage, then empties it for the next shower. She can discuss finding an open spot, testing homemade tools, or how she discovered the misleading water source.

posts.caption: Packing test complete: my old suitcase still fits everything. I had to sit on it for the last inch, which counts as successful negotiation.
posts.translationZh: 試裝完成：舊行李箱還裝得下所有東西。最後差一點點，我坐上去才拉起來，就當這次協商成功。
posts.imageAlt: Bella testing the zipper of her packed suitcase in a spare room.
posts.storyContext: After measuring her suitcase instead of buying a larger one, Bella tries packing it in the spare room after work. A bulky jumper is the main obstacle, and a brief sit on the closed case helps the zipper meet. She can discuss overpacking, the clothes she refuses to leave behind, or whether a test pack ever survives the actual trip.

posts.caption: This morning I used the stairs instead of pressing the lift button again. Seven landings gave my impatience something useful to count.
posts.translationZh: 今天早上改走樓梯，不再多按一次電梯按鈕。七個樓梯平台，正好讓我的沒耐性有東西可以數。
posts.imageAlt: Felix counting landings on an empty external office staircase.
posts.storyContext: Remembering yesterday's pointless second press of the lift button, Felix chooses the external stairs on his morning commute. He counts seven landings and arrives a little warmer than planned. He can discuss how he estimates a quicker route, the difference between waiting and moving, or whether he will make the same choice with a heavier bag.

posts.caption: My balance practice met its real test: rain overshoes. I stayed upright, then noticed the left one was on my right shoe.
posts.translationZh: 平衡練習遇上真正的考驗：雨天鞋套。我站穩了，才發現左邊那隻套在右腳。
posts.imageAlt: Finn checking an overshoe beside an empty entrance bench.
posts.storyContext: Finn follows yesterday's balance success with a practical test before work: putting on rain overshoes while standing. He stays steady, then notices that one overshoe is on the wrong foot. He sits at the entrance bench to swap them. He can discuss balance with awkward footwear, taking time to check a small job, or the everyday uses of his practice.

posts.caption: I brought yesterday's pickles to lunch. The one I liked least turns out to be excellent with a very boring egg.
posts.translationZh: 我把昨天的醃菜帶來配午餐。原本最不喜歡的那款，搭上平凡到不行的蛋，居然很合。
posts.imageAlt: Hugo pairs leftover pickles with a boiled egg in a quiet workplace kitchenette.
posts.storyContext: Hugo brings the remaining three pickles from dinner to his workplace lunch. One that tasted too sharp on its own works surprisingly well with a boiled egg. He saves the other combinations for later rather than ranking them immediately. He can discuss foods that improve with the right partner, lunch leftovers, or which pairing deserves another chance.

posts.caption: I checked yesterday's light study against my pastels at lunch. That innocent white patch has somehow used up three shades of grey.
posts.translationZh: 午休拿昨天的光線習作對照粉彩。那塊看起來無辜的白色，居然用掉了三種灰。
posts.imageAlt: Iris compares unmarked pastel swatches with a small light study in her studio.
posts.storyContext: Iris takes the small garage-light study into her studio during lunch and compares it with plain pastel swatches. The pale area needs several greys rather than one white, which changes how she wants to finish the edge. She can discuss the colours hidden in ordinary light, choosing materials, or whether the unfinished corner should stay visible.

posts.caption: I left my audiobook paused for the rest of the walk to work. A loose drain cover supplied a surprisingly regular percussion part.
posts.translationZh: 走去上班的剩下那段路，我都沒把有聲書打開。一塊鬆動的排水蓋倒是提供了意外規律的打擊樂。
posts.imageAlt: Isla pauses beside a station footpath with her headphones resting around her neck.
posts.storyContext: Isla leaves her audiobook paused again on the walk to work, following yesterday's quiet stretch after a chapter ending. Beyond the station, a loose drain cover clinks beneath one shoe, briefly giving her footsteps a different rhythm. She can discuss the sounds of familiar routes, listening habits, or where she will resume the chapter.

posts.caption: I folded last night's enormous scarf shadow back into my tiny hallway basket. The actual scarf seems far less ambitious in daylight.
posts.translationZh: 我把昨晚那條超巨大圍巾影子的本尊，摺回玄關的小籃子。白天看來，它本人沒那麼有野心。
posts.imageAlt: Luna folds a long scarf beside a small basket in her apartment vestibule.
posts.storyContext: Luna remembers the long scarf shadow on the footbridge while putting the scarf away before work. In the apartment vestibule, the fabric fits neatly into a small basket, which makes its dramatic nighttime shape seem unlikely. She can discuss objects transformed by light, familiar things seen differently, or where another long shadow might appear.

posts.caption: I got the headlamp strap straight, then put it in a pouch that wouldn't zip. It's going back in a bigger pouch.
posts.translationZh: 我把頭燈帶整理好了，裝進收納袋才發現拉鍊拉不起來。還是換個大一點的袋子再還吧。
posts.imageAlt: Max fits a borrowed headlamp into a fabric pouch beside an equipment locker.
posts.storyContext: Max is ready to return the cleaned, charged headlamp after work. At the equipment locker, he discovers that the tidy strap still will not let it fit inside his smallest pouch. He finds a larger one rather than forcing the zip. He can talk about borrowed gear, useful packing habits, or the outdoor kit that always takes more room than expected.

posts.caption: I folded the borrowed runner with its darker edge outside. Now I can ask about that stripe without unfolding the whole thing again.
posts.translationZh: 我把借來的桌旗折好，特地讓顏色較深的那邊露在外面。這樣想問那道條紋時，就不用整條再攤開一次了。
posts.imageAlt: Maya holds a neatly folded woven runner at a quiet apartment doorway.
posts.storyContext: Maya returns the borrowed runner after work, folding its darker edge outward so she remembers what she wanted to ask. The uneven fading has made her curious about where it used to sit and which side faced the light. She waits alone at the closed doorway. She can discuss fabrics with a history, thoughtful ways to return borrowed things, or the clues wear leaves behind.

posts.caption: I sent a second voice note with the actual detail. Three seconds long. A surprisingly small sequel to all that careful waiting.
posts.translationZh: 我補傳了一則語音，這次有講到重點了。只有三秒。等了那麼久，續集意外地短。
posts.imageAlt: Noah records a short voice note alone on a quiet stair landing.
posts.storyContext: After yesterday's carefully timed but incomplete voice note, Noah finds a quiet stair landing before work and records the missing detail. He only needed to say to bring a bowl, so the follow-up lasts three seconds. The tiny correction makes him smile. He can talk about voice notes, the details people forget, or finding a quiet spot during a noisy day.

posts.caption: I checked the cupboard after closing that sale basket. I already own the thing. Apparently, storage is my most effective discount code.
posts.translationZh: 關掉特價購物籃後，我去翻了櫃子。那東西我早就有了。看來收納櫃才是我最有效的折扣碼。
posts.imageAlt: Oscar finds an unused folding shopping bag inside a quiet storage cupboard.
posts.storyContext: Oscar checks a storage cupboard after deciding the sale delivery charge was not worth it. He finds the folding shopping bag he had nearly bought, still in good condition behind some folded blankets. The discovery settles the question completely. He can discuss forgotten possessions, shopping arithmetic, or how cupboards occasionally provide better deals than sales.

posts.caption: Sideways did it: I got the oversized repair manual through the doorway. A promising improvement on yesterday's return slot.
posts.translationZh: 橫著抱就行了：我把那本超大維修手冊帶進了門。比起昨天的還書口，這次的進展很有希望。
posts.imageAlt: Ryan carries a large closed manual sideways through a quiet book-return vestibule.
posts.storyContext: Ryan brings the oversized repair manual back during his lunch break. After its failed encounter with the return slot, he is taking it through the entrance to return at the desk. The weight has become more memorable than the repair advice. He can discuss unwieldy library finds and the repair he originally needed help with.

posts.caption: I gave my five-minute plan one actual job: unplug the idle charger. Finished before I could redesign the evening.
posts.translationZh: 我替那個五分鐘計畫分配了一件正事：拔掉沒在用的充電器。在我重新規劃整個晚上之前，完成了。
posts.imageAlt: Theo places an unplugged idle charger in a small tray by a home utility cabinet.
posts.storyContext: Theo follows up his overthought five-minute planning session by choosing a task small enough to finish immediately after work. He unplugs an unused charger and puts it away rather than designing another elaborate schedule. He can discuss realistic task sizes, stray chargers and the difference between useful preparation and enjoyable tinkering.

posts.caption: I hung my almost-dry umbrella by its strap at work. One last drop waited until I put my shoe underneath.
posts.translationZh: 我到公司後，把差不多乾了的傘用腕帶掛起來。最後一滴水，偏偏等到我的鞋子移過去才滴下來。
posts.imageAlt: Yuna hangs a folded umbrella by its wrist strap in a quiet office cloakroom.
posts.storyContext: Yuna follows yesterday’s umbrella-dryer experiment by hanging the folded umbrella where the last trapped water can drain. A single delayed drop catches her shoe as she steps away. She can talk about rainy commutes, how she dries small everyday things and the minor surprises she notices before work begins.

posts.caption: I put the scarf's hitchhiking sock in a paper envelope to return it. It now has a more organised commute than I do.
posts.translationZh: 我把搭圍巾便車的那隻襪子放進紙信封，準備拿去歸還。它現在的通勤安排比我還有條理。
posts.imageAlt: Zoe carries a plain paper envelope with a sock peeking out beside empty building mail cubbies.
posts.storyContext: Zoe turns the stray sock from the dryer into a small return errand before work. She tucks it into a plain envelope so it cannot attach itself to another scarf on the way. She can discuss how she will locate its owner, laundry mix-ups and the unexpectedly formal treatment of an ordinary sock.

posts.caption: My homemade rain gauge had water in it on a dry morning. Found the sprinkler reaching it, so I've moved it beyond the planters.
posts.translationZh: 明明一早沒下雨，我自製的雨量筒裡卻有水。原來灑水器噴得到，我把它移到花盆外側去了。
posts.imageAlt: Ada holds an unmarked homemade rain gauge beside planters at the edge of a sheltered parking bay.
posts.storyContext: Ada made a simple rain gauge from a straight transparent collection tube mounted in a small wire holder. Checking it before work, she finds water despite the dry morning and notices that the planter sprinkler reaches the spot. She moves the gauge into the open beyond the planters. She can discuss how she assembled it, a better place to collect rain, or whether the next shower gives a more useful reading.

posts.caption: The sale nearly convinced me I needed a bigger suitcase. I measured mine first. Turns out I mostly need to pack fewer jumpers.
posts.translationZh: 折扣差點說服我買一咖更大的行李箱。我先量了現有這咖，結果我主要需要的，好像是少帶幾件毛衣。
posts.imageAlt: Bella looks back at a suitcase while measuring its width on an apartment landing.
posts.storyContext: A November 11 discount makes Bella consider replacing her suitcase. Before ordering, she measures the one she owns and compares its space with the pile of bulky knitwear she usually packs. She has left the purchase undecided. She can discuss overpacking habits, what actually needs to come on a short trip, or whether a tempting sale changes a useful decision.

posts.caption: Pressed the lift button twice before remembering that once is the full instruction. My lunch and I are still waiting.
posts.translationZh: 電梯按鈕按了兩下，才想起按一次就已經把指令交代完了。我和午餐還是得繼續等。
posts.imageAlt: Felix waits beside a lift with a lunch container in a plain office lobby.
posts.storyContext: Felix notices himself pressing the lift call button again even though it is already lit. He has a short lunch break and is impatient with a machine that has already received the message. He settles into waiting with his food container in hand. He can discuss whether repeated presses ever do anything, his usual lunch timing, or small habits that persist despite knowing better.

posts.caption: The balance practice paid off: one sock went on standing up. For the other one, I accepted the chair's help.
posts.translationZh: 平衡練習有成果了：一隻襪子是站著穿好的。另一隻，我接受了椅子的協助。
posts.imageAlt: Finn balances on one foot while pulling on a sock beside his bedroom chair.
posts.storyContext: Finn notices an everyday use for last week’s balance practice while getting dressed for work. He manages one sock on one foot without sitting down, then sensibly uses the bedroom chair for the other. The new progress happens away from the beam and does not require a training session. He can talk about his steadier side, morning routines, or little signs that practice has carried over.

posts.caption: Three kinds of pickles with dinner, because I couldn't choose. I've since learned that choosing was the sensible part of the plan.
posts.translationZh: 晚餐配了三種醃菜，因為實在選不出來。吃到現在才發現，原來先做選擇是有道理的。
posts.imageAlt: Hugo sits at a home dining booth with three small pickle dishes and a bowl of rice.
posts.storyContext: Hugo sets out pickled red cabbage, pickled mustard greens and sweet pickled ginger beside a plain rice bowl. He means to compare them, but keeps changing his mind as the flavours overlap. A generous serving of rice restores the balance. He can discuss small side dishes, contrasting textures and how much is enough for a meal for one.

posts.caption: That strip of garage light looked white until I put it on paper. My little study now contains four colours and barely any garage.
posts.translationZh: 車庫那道光本來看起來是白的，一畫到紙上就不是了。這張小習作現在有四種顏色，卻幾乎沒有車庫。
posts.imageAlt: Iris makes a small oil-pastel colour study of light crossing a bare parking-garage pillar.
posts.storyContext: A fluorescent strip reflected across a matte concrete pillar catches Iris's attention on her way home. From a clear pedestrian recess in the garage, she uses oil pastels to record its pale green, violet and yellow edges. The drawing becomes more abstract than planned. She can discuss how artificial light changes familiar surfaces and when a quick colour note feels finished.

posts.caption: My audiobook chapter ended at the crossing. I left the next one for later and listened to the wind for a minute.
posts.translationZh: 有聲書的一章剛好在人行道口播完。我把下一章留到晚點，先聽了一分鐘的風聲。
posts.imageAlt: Isla waits on a pedestrian refuge with her earbuds lowered and her attention on the opposite pavement.
posts.storyContext: Walking home after work, Isla reaches a long crossing just as an audiobook chapter ends. She decides not to start the next one until she is across. The ordinary wait feels unusually spacious without a voice filling it. She notices the wind moving a loose sleeve and can talk about listening habits, chapter endings and the tiny gaps that usually get filled automatically.

posts.caption: The streetlight gave my scarf a tail three metres long. I swished it once on the way home. A very small comet, running slightly late.
posts.translationZh: 路燈幫我的圍巾加了一條三公尺長的尾巴。回家路上甩了一下。是一顆有點晚歸的小彗星。
posts.imageAlt: Luna glances back at the long shadow of her trailing scarf on an empty pedestrian footbridge.
posts.storyContext: Luna crosses a quiet footbridge after an evening errand and notices the long scarf shadow stretching behind her. One quick swish changes its shape more than she expects. She pauses for a second look, then wraps the scarf snugly again for the rest of the walk. She can discuss streetlight shadows, small night-time observations and the difference a single light source makes.

posts.caption: I'm returning the borrowed headlamp clean and charged. The strap needed untwisting first. It had apparently been packing itself.
posts.translationZh: 借來的頭燈要擦乾淨、充好電再還。得先把帶子解開，它顯然有自己的一套收納方式。
posts.imageAlt: Max checks a borrowed headlamp while sorting outdoor kit on a sheltered utility balcony.
posts.storyContext: Before work, Max sorts a few small outdoor items so he can return a borrowed headlamp that evening. The lamp is ready, but its elastic strap has twisted around a buckle in the storage pouch. He puts the rest of the kit aside and works it straight. He can discuss what makes a useful borrowed item, how he packs small gear, and what is worth keeping ready by the door.

posts.caption: This borrowed runner has a darker stripe along one edge. I keep turning it around to imagine the sunny table it used to sit on.
posts.translationZh: 借來的桌旗有一邊顏色比較深。我一直換方向擺，想像它以前是在什麼樣的向陽桌邊待著。
posts.imageAlt: Maya turns to examine a less-faded stripe along a woven table runner spread across her dining table.
posts.storyContext: Maya borrows a woven runner to see whether its size suits her small table. One edge is noticeably darker than the rest, perhaps because it was once tucked away from sunlight. She changes its position while imagining the room it came from. She can discuss how useful objects change with time, ask the owner about its previous home, or decide which end suits her table best.

posts.caption: I waited for a van to pass before recording a voice note. Forgot the useful bit, so I sent the hello and remembered it straight afterward.
posts.translationZh: 等一台廂型車經過才錄語音訊息，結果把正事忘了。先傳了聲哈囉，傳完才立刻想起來。
posts.imageAlt: Noah pauses with a phone after recording a short voice note in an empty covered lane.
posts.storyContext: On his way to work, Noah pauses under a covered lane to record a quick voice note. He waits for a passing engine to fade, then finds that the opening greeting has displaced the practical thing he meant to say. The detail returns as soon as he sends it, so a second brief message follows. He can discuss keeping in touch, little memory gaps, or how different a voice can feel from a typed note.

posts.caption: The discount saved less than delivery cost. I've closed the basket, having briefly enjoyed the sensation of being good at shopping.
posts.translationZh: 折扣省下的錢還不夠付運費。我把購物車關了，至少短暫享受過很會買東西的感覺。
posts.imageAlt: Oscar closes a plain laptop at a home window desk after checking an online order total.
posts.storyContext: A November 11 offer tempts Oscar to replace a small desk item that still works. He checks the final total and notices that delivery costs more than the discount saves. He closes the basket and keeps the item he has. He can discuss whether the replacement was needed, the arithmetic of small bargains, or how much comparison is reasonable for an ordinary purchase.

posts.caption: The repair manual won't fit through the library return slot. I borrowed it to get things done at home. One more trip to the desk, then.
posts.translationZh: 修繕手冊塞不進圖書館還書口。本來借它是想在家多做點事。好吧，再去櫃台一趟。
posts.imageAlt: Ryan pauses with an oversized plain-bound manual beside a narrow library return slot.
posts.storyContext: Ryan stops at the library on the way home with a large household repair manual. The thick binding will not pass through the side return slot without forcing it, so he decides to take it to the desk instead. He has already found a useful diagram for a future project. He can discuss what he learned, oversize books and errands that turn out to have an extra step.

posts.caption: Set a five-minute timer to plan my evening. I used most of it deciding what could actually fit into an evening.
posts.translationZh: 設了五分鐘計時器，打算安排一下晚上要做的事。大半時間都在想，一個晚上到底實際裝得下多少事。
posts.imageAlt: Theo smiles as he sets a small mechanical timer on the shelf beside him inside a quiet focus booth.
posts.storyContext: Theo uses an empty focus booth after work to make a short plan before heading home. He sets a mechanical timer for five minutes and realises his list contains more tasks than the evening can hold. By the end he has chosen one small repair and left the rest for later. He can discuss estimating time, choosing a useful stopping point and why a shorter plan may be easier to follow.

posts.caption: The umbrella dryer made mine almost dry. I gave it one more pass, mostly because the little rollers were oddly satisfying.
posts.translationZh: 雨傘除水機把我的傘弄得差不多乾了。我又多滾了一次，主要是那幾個小滾輪莫名療癒。
posts.imageAlt: Yuna guides a closed umbrella through absorbent rollers at an empty station entrance.
posts.storyContext: A light shower follows Yuna to the station after work. She notices a simple umbrella dryer at the entrance and carefully passes her closed umbrella through its absorbent rollers. Most of the drops disappear on the first pass, but she makes a second slow one before putting the umbrella away. She can discuss small conveniences, rainy commutes and the unexpectedly pleasant feel of an ordinary mechanism.

posts.caption: Found a sock clinging to my scarf after the dryer. I nearly wore it outside, which would have been a very specific accessory.
posts.translationZh: 烘完衣服才發現，一隻襪子黏在圍巾上。差點就這樣戴出門了，也算是風格非常明確的配件。
posts.imageAlt: Zoe gently pulls a static-clinging sock from a scarf at an empty laundrette folding ledge.
posts.storyContext: Zoe collects a small load at the laundrette after work and drapes a dry scarf over her arm. A sock has attached itself to the fabric with static and stays there until she starts folding. She peels it away before heading out, amused at how close it came to joining her outfit. She can discuss sorting laundry, unusual sock hiding places and whether a final check saves more trouble than it takes.

posts.caption: My flask strap kept sliding off my shoulder. One extra loop of webbing later, I can carry lunch without doing a little shrug every few steps.
posts.translationZh: 保溫瓶的背帶一直從肩上滑下來。多加一圈織帶之後，帶午餐出門終於不用每走幾步就聳一下肩。
posts.imageAlt: Ada tests an extra webbing loop on her flask strap in a quiet office supply nook.
posts.storyContext: Ada uses her lunch break to add a short webbing keeper to the carrying strap of her flask. The strap used to slide loose whenever she walked quickly, and the first test is simply carrying it across the room. She can talk about where to position the keeper, why some bag straps never stay put, or whether the fix still works over a thicker coat.

posts.caption: That caramel came wrapped beautifully. I've managed to unwrap half of it and wear the rest on one finger.
posts.translationZh: 那塊焦糖包得好漂亮。我成功拆開了一半，另一半現在戴在我的手指上。
posts.imageAlt: Bella pauses over a sticky caramel wrapper at a quiet confectionery counter.
posts.storyContext: Bella stops for one soft caramel on the way home. The sweet has stuck to its plain paper wrapper, turning a quick treat into a slow negotiation. She has found a quiet end of the counter to finish unwrapping it before putting her gloves back on. The scene offers talk about favorite chewy sweets, cold-weather snacks, and food packaging that demands more patience than expected.

posts.caption: One clap in the tiled passage sounded much bigger than mine. I moved two steps and lost the echo completely.
posts.translationZh: 在磁磚通道裡拍了一下手，聲音大得像不是我拍的。往旁邊走兩步，回音卻整個不見了。
posts.imageAlt: Felix tests a small echo with a clap inside an empty tiled pedestrian underpass.
posts.storyContext: On his way home, Felix hears an unexpectedly full echo in a tiled underpass and tests it with a single clap. Moving a little changes the sound more than he expected. He waits until the passage is empty to compare two spots. He can discuss where the sound seemed to return from, why corners change it, or other small observations that interrupt a routine commute.

posts.caption: Ten clean catches against the wall was the plan. I got nine, then spent the tenth chasing the ball under a chair.
posts.translationZh: 原本打算對牆連接十球。接到第九球了，第十球則變成追進椅子底下找球。
posts.imageAlt: Finn reaches for a small practice ball beside a folding chair in a quiet garage.
posts.storyContext: After work, Finn sets himself a small coordination challenge: ten one-handed catches from a gentle wall rebound. The ball slips away just before he reaches the target and rolls under a chair. He is keeping the exercise playful rather than restarting the entire count. He can discuss which hand is harder, whether nine is enough for tonight, or the household objects that become accidental obstacles.
